summary: Defines MIB objects for managing ATM interfaces, devices, and services beyond those in the ATM-MIB of RFC 2515. They add support for ATM switched and permanent virtual connections. It is a proposed standard.

eli5.summary: ATM is an older network type. This memo adds more things a manager can look at on those networks.

questions: what is an atm svc cross-connect
what is an atm vp tunnel
subtitle: Extra SNMP objects for managing ATM switched and permanent virtual connections, on top of the ATM-MIB.

tldr.problem: The ATM-MIB of RFC 2515 did not cover everything needed to manage ATM interfaces, in particular switched virtual connections (SVCs) and richer support for permanent virtual connections (PVCs).
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3606 defines the ATM2-MIB module, which adds 21 tables for switches, network services and hosts, covering SVC cross-connects, signalling, addresses, statistics, ILMI and failing PVCs, plus one PVC failure notification.
tldr.outcome: Managers get a way to monitor SVC cross-connects, signalling activity, per-VPL and per-VCL cell counters and failing PVCs without polling every row of the base tables.

today: RFC 3606 is a Proposed Standard from November 2003, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Purpose and Scope
sections.content:
RFC 3606 supplements the ATM-MIB of RFC 2515. It adds objects needed to manage ATM interfaces in three areas: ATM Switch Support, ATM Service Support and ATM Host Support. It also adds trap support.

The module is an extension, not a replacement. Managing ATM interfaces, links and cross-connects still needs other MIB modules, for example MIB II for interfaces (RFC 2863), and the DS3 and SONET MIBs for the physical interfaces. This MIB also requires the ATM-MIB itself and the ATM-specific textual conventions of RFC 2514.

The motivating case is endpoint applications such as LAN Emulation or Classical IP-over-ATM clients and servers. They set up SVCs and PVCs to exchange control and data, and their agents must tell the network manager which connections are in use and which applications use them.
sections.eli5: An older rule book listed what a manager could check on ATM networks. This memo adds more pages to it.

sections.title: Links, Connections and Segments
sections.content:
The memo defines six terms used throughout the MIB. A Virtual Path Link (VPL) joins two adjacent devices. A Virtual Path Connection (VPC) is the whole path between the end hosts. A Virtual Path Segment is a part of a connection between two intermediate points, for example between two switches. The same three ideas exist for virtual channels: VCL, VCC and VC Segment.

The figures in the RFC use Host1, SwitchA, SwitchB, SwitchC and Host2 in a chain. Each link between neighbours is a link, the whole span from Host1 to Host2 is the connection, and the stretch from SwitchA to SwitchC is a segment.

Cross-connects are modeled with a low and a high port. The interface with the lower ifIndex is the low one, and traffic is described as flowing low to high and high to low.
sections.eli5: Think of a relay race. Each hand-off between neighbours is a link, the whole race is the connection, and a middle stretch is a segment.

sections.title: The Tables
sections.content:
The module consists of 21 tables. Table 1 of the RFC marks each table as applying to hosts, switches, services or a combination. The main families are:

  • SVC cross-connects (atmSvcVpCrossConnectTable, atmSvcVcCrossConnectTable): read-only monitoring of switched cross-connects, including Soft PVPs and Soft PVCs, with a row-status object that is writable so a connection can be torn down. The PVC equivalents stay in RFC 2515. A point-to-point cross-connect is one entry, one with N leafs is N entries, and a multipoint-to-multipoint one with N parties is N(N-1)/2 entries that share an index.
  • Signalling: atmSigStatTable counters for the signalling entity, atmSigSupportTable showing which information elements (such as calling party number) are enabled, and atmSigDescrParamTable holding reusable signalling parameters for SVCs.
  • Addresses: registered addresses per interface and mappings between ATM addresses and VPI/VCI values in both directions.
  • Statistics: cell counters per VPL and per VCL, and AAL5 statistics per VCC.
  • ILMI: a service registry, network prefixes and switch addresses.
  • Failing PVCs: lists of the permanent links that are in trouble.

Two counters are also added for leaf-initiated join setup requests and setup failures.
sections.eli5: It is a big binder of forms. One form tracks connections, another counts calls, another lists addresses, and another counts cells passing through.

sections.title: Statistics, Logical Ports and ILMI
sections.content:
Cell counters. The per-VPL and per-VCL tables count valid ATM cells, which include user and OAM cells but exclude physical-layer cells such as idle cells and unassigned cells. Incoming and outgoing cells are counted as a total and as CLP=0 cells. The CLP=1 count is derived by subtraction, and cells tagged on output are counted separately. On a switch with no traffic policing, the Output Tagged Cells counter is always zero.

VP tunnels. The interface type ATM Logical Port (ifType=80) represents a VP Tunnel, a VPL used as a trunk between devices that are not physically adjacent. One use is tunneling across a public network that does not support signalling. To create one through SNMP, a manager creates a VPL, sets atmVplLogicalPortDef to isLogicalIf, and the agent then creates the new interface row.

Interface type and side. atmIntfConfigType and atmIntfConfigSide configure the connection setup procedure and which side the entity plays. Values include ituDss2, atmfUni3Dot1, atmfPnni1Dot0 and atmfBici2Dot0. With autoConfig, the type comes from ILMI auto-configuration. PNNI and BICI are symmetric, so no side is set. Read-back objects report the actual type and side.

Negotiated VCI. Each side configures a minimum SVCC VCI, and both interfaces end up using the larger of the two. In the RFC's example, 32 and 40 negotiate to 40 on both interfaces, while 32 and 32 stay at 32.

Service registry. atmIlmiSrvcRegTable tells hosts where network services such as the LAN Emulation Configuration Server, ATMARP server or NHRP server are found. A row can apply to one interface or, with index 0, to any interface.
sections.eli5: The switch counts every cell that passes, can build a private tunnel for other connections to ride in, and keeps a phone book of helpful services for its neighbours.

sections.title: Failing PVCs and the Trap
sections.content:
Polling every row of the VPL and VCL tables to find broken permanent connections is slow and resource intensive. The memo adds shortcuts. The counter atmIntfPvcFailures and the gauges atmIntfCurrentlyFailingPVpls and atmIntfCurrentlyFailingPVcls give a quick per-interface status. The tables atmCurrentlyFailingPVplTable and atmCurrentlyFailingPVclTable list exactly which links are in trouble.

The single notification, atmIntfPvcFailuresTrap, is generated just after a PVPL or PVCL leaves the up state. The manager then reads the failing tables to see which ones. Traps are rate limited: those occurring within atmIntfPvcNotificationInterval of a previous trap for the same interface are suppressed, so managers should keep polling the tables for at least that long to track the network.
sections.eli5: Instead of checking every light bulb in a building, you look at a short list of the ones that are out, and a bell rings when a new one goes dark.

sections.title: Conformance
sections.content:
The compliance statement atm2MIBCompliance makes atmCommonGroup mandatory for all. Other groups depend on the role: atmSwitchServcGroup is mandatory for a switch or service that implements ATM interfaces, the switch-only group is optional for switches, and the service group applies to systems implementing a service. The common statistics group is required for systems that keep per-VPC or per-VCC counters, and the notification group is optional for switches and services.

For several row-status objects, write access is not required and only the active(1) value needs to be supported.
sections.eli5: Everyone must have the basic forms, and switches and services must have a few extra ones that fit their job.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC lists all 21 tables with their sensitivity. Deleting VP or VC cross-connects, changing signalling or ILMI configuration, and altering logical port or interface configuration are the main risks of read-write and read-create objects. Some read-only tables can also be sensitive, so GET and NOTIFY access should be controlled.

SNMP versions before SNMPv3 did not include adequate security, and even a secure network gives no control over who on it may GET or SET these objects. The RFC RECOMMENDS SNMPv3 with its cryptographic mechanisms and says deploying earlier versions is NOT RECOMMENDED.
sections.eli5: Some of these controls can tear down connections, so only trusted people should be allowed to use them.
